title: Andrew (30 November)
hook: the first called, who brought his brother Peter; patron of Scotland and of Constantinople

segments.voice: Yesterday, Catherine. Your line was wisdom and courage. And a week's end, so look back at the company: Philippine praying, Mary given as a child, Cecilia singing, Columban on the road, Miguel Pro with open arms, Catherine with her book. Day one thousand fifty.

"Come and see." That's the whole invitation. Two men have been standing with John the Baptist when Jesus walks past, and John points him out. The two men leave John and walk after Jesus, saying nothing yet. Jesus turns and asks what they're looking for. They answer with a question: where do you live? He says, come and see. They spend the rest of the day with him. One of those two men is named in the next verse. Today, Andrew.
screen: `TWO MEN FOLLOW.` → `WHERE DO YOU LIVE?` → `COME AND SEE.`

segments.voice: Look at how John's gospel introduces him. Not as Andrew, the disciple. As "Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter." Even on his big day, he's somebody's brother. And what does he do with his afternoon with Jesus? He goes home. In the Douay-Rheims: "He findeth first his brother Simon, and saith to him: We have found the Messias." Then the verse ends simply: "And he brought him to Jesus." That's Andrew's pattern, and John's gospel shows it more than once. When a huge crowd is hungry, Andrew is the one who points out a boy with five barley loaves and two fishes, even while wondering out loud what good so little could do. When some Greeks come looking for Jesus, they ask Philip, and Philip goes to Andrew, and the two of them bring the request to Jesus. Andrew doesn't give the big speeches. Peter does that. Andrew makes introductions. Eastern Christians give him a title: the First-Called. Tradition says he preached around the Black Sea and was crucified on an X-shaped cross, which is why Scotland, which claims him as patron, flies a white X on blue. The church of Constantinople honors him as its founder, the way Rome honors his brother Peter. In recent times, on Andrew's feast, a delegation from Rome visits the patriarch in Istanbul, and on Peter's feast a delegation from the patriarch visits Rome. The brothers are still bringing people to each other.
screen: `ANDREW, THE BROTHER OF SIMON PETER.` · `HE FINDS HIS BROTHER FIRST.` · `A BOY WITH LOAVES, SOME GREEKS.` · `TWO BROTHERS, ROME AND CONSTANTINOPLE.` · then, large: `AND HE BROUGHT HIM TO JESUS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: be the one who introduces. Settle and breathe. Think of two people you know who don't know each other, but should. Maybe they share a worry, or a hobby, or a hard season. Hold both faces in mind for a while. Picture them meeting, and what they might give each other. If you pray, you can bring both of them to God by name, the way Andrew brought his brother. If you don't, simply decide how you'll make the introduction. The bell holds the time.
Andrew. Simon Peter's brother, called the First-Called, who spent one afternoon with Jesus and then went straight home to get his brother.
Your line: he brought his brother. Today, send one message that connects two people who would be good for each other, and then step back. Day one thousand fifty.

howItsDone: The feast of Saint Andrew, apostle, is kept on 30 November; it is a great feast in Scotland and for the church of Constantinople, and the season of Advent begins close to it.

go back and report to John the Baptist

original.note: Greek: the First-Called, the title Eastern Christians give Andrew.

trapdoor: what you thought: Peter's quieter brother.
what it means: the one who keeps bringing people to Jesus: his brother, a boy with bread, some Greeks.
what a scholar hears: the First-Called, patron of Constantinople as Peter is of Rome; the two churches visit each other on the brothers' feasts.

notes: Audit (fresh pass): Douay-Rheims John 1:39-42 wording and numbering, John 6:8-9 and 12:20-22 checked; week-end review consistent with day 1043's week end. No change.
Week's end (day 1050): the review looks back at days 1044–1049.

Confirm Challoner verse numbering and wording: 'Come and see' (1:39), 'Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter' (1:40), 'He findeth first his brother Simon, and saith to him: We have found the Messias' (1:41), 'And he brought him to Jesus' (1:42).
'Five barley loaves and two fishes' is from John 6:9; confirm.
Tradition (not scripture): preaching around the Black Sea, X-shaped cross, Scotland's saltire, Constantinople's claim to Andrew as founder. All attributed to tradition; confirm phrasing.
The exchange of delegations (Rome to the Ecumenical Patriarchate on 30 November, Constantinople to Rome on 29 June) stated as 'in recent times'; confirm it is current.
Index hook calls him 'the first called'; the script attributes the title to Eastern Christians rather than stating it as fact.

Editor pass: John 6:8–9 has Andrew point out the boy, not bring him forward; teach and match fixed. Hook no longer tells the listener how it feels to trail someone, and the invented 'awkwardly' is cut.
